[Lähde: TechCrunch]
For once, SpaceX is ahead of schedule: Elon Musk’s space and AI conglomerate officially confirmed that it has raised $75 billion from the sale of its shares to its underwriters, who are set to begin marketing the company on the Nasdaq stock exchange Friday.

SpaceX priced its 555.6 million shares at $135 each, the company said in an update on its website. That makes SpaceX officially the largest IPO in history, easily eclipsing the $24.9 billion in funds raised by Saudi Aramco during its 2019 public markets debut. ---

[Lähde: New York Post]
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Elon Musk’s SpaceX has officially priced its record initial public offering at $135 per share, catapulting the rocket firm among the world’s most valuable companies ahead of its Friday debut.

The hotly anticipated IPO raised $75 billion while selling 555.6 million shares, according to a statement posted on SpaceX’s website on Thursday afternoon. The company will trade on the Nasdaq Composite Index under the ticket “SPCX.”

It’s going public at an approximately $1.77 trillion valuation – which will instantly establish it as the seventh-largest US firm. It will be more valuable than tech mainstays like Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta and Musk’s other company, electric car maker Tesla.

The SpaceX IPO shattered the previous record set by Saudi Aramco’s IPO, which raised $29.4 billion in 2019.

Musk himself is now close to becoming the first trillionaire in history. His personal net worth was $792 billion as of Thursday, according to Forbes.

SpaceX’s board has already teed up a massive pay package for Musk tied to the company’s success. The South African billionaire can earn 1 billion Class B shares that will vest if the company establishes “a permanent human colony on Mars with at least one million inhabitants.” The plan marks an unusual instance of a company tying executive pay to metrics other than typical financial ones.

There are also rewards for hitting a $7.5 trillion market cap and building “non-Earth-based data centers.

After the IPO, Musk will control about 82% of SpaceX, according to Reuters.

The public debut drew massive interest from retail investors who submitted more than $100 billion in purchase orders, according to Bloomberg.

The IPO was four times oversubscribed, meaning there were four times as many purchase orders as there were available shares.

While SpaceX is expected to make at least 20% of shares available to individuals in its IPO, that number would still mean that just a fraction of run-of-the-mill investors who want to buy shares will actually be able to do so, with the rest going to big institutions.

Some crypto traders are reportedly taking a bullish view of SpaceX’s prospects.

Futures contracts tied to SpaceX’s stock that are sold on crypto platforms Hyperliquid and Binance were trading at $165 as of Thursday morning, according to Bloomberg.

Despite the massive demand, some market watchers have warned that SpaceX’s balance sheet is too weak to justify its valuation.

[Lähde: International Business Times Singapore]
SpaceX is finally heading to public markets in one of the most closely watched IPOs in history, with trading expected to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX. But while retail investors are being given unusual access, buying into the company is not as simple, or as guaranteed, as many suggest.

Here's what investors need to know about whether you can actually buy SpaceX stock, how the IPO works, and the risks behind the hype.

SpaceX is set to debut at a price of around $135 per share, aiming to raise roughly $75 billion and value the company at about $1.75 trillion, according to multiple market reports.

That would make it the largest IPO in history, far surpassing previous record listings.

The company will sell roughly 555 million shares, with trading expected to begin once the IPO is officially launched on Nasdaq.

"The point is that in the grand scheme of the U.S. equity market, these share issues are surprisingly digestible," Gavekal Research analyst Will Denyer wrote in a June 3 note. He added that "any drag on U.S. equity performance from the liquidity drain should be short-lived."

Yes, but access is limited and competitive. Unlike a traditional public listing where most shares go to institutions, SpaceX is reportedly allocating a rare 20%–30% of shares to retail investors, a significantly higher share than typical IPOs.

Retail investors may be able to participate through selected brokerage platforms, including major names such as Fidelity, Robinhood, E*TRADE, Charles Schwab and SoFi.

However, eligibility alone does not guarantee allocation. Demand has already reportedly exceeded supply multiple times over, meaning many applicants may receive only partial shares, or none at all.

What Happens If You Miss the IPO Allocation?

According to Reuters, if you do not receive shares during the IPO window, you can still buy SpaceX stock once it begins trading on the open market. But there is a catch: analysts expect significant volatility on day one and beyond, driven by heavy retail demand, limited available float, speculative valuation concerns and large institutional positioning.

Some forecasts warn that IPO enthusiasm could lead to sharp price swings once trading begins

SpaceX is not the only company seeking substantial investor capital. According to Gavekal, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Alphabet collectively seek roughly $380 billion in public-market funding.

payload.title: SpaceX hinnoitteli osakkeensa 135 dollariin ennätyssuuressa listautumisannissa
payload.summary: SpaceX on hinnoitellut listautumisantinsa osakkeet 135 dollariin kappaleelta. Yhtiön kerrotaan keränneen osakemyynnillä noin 75 miljardia dollaria ennen Nasdaq-kaupankäynnin alkua.
payload.content:
SpaceX on hinnoitellut listautumisantinsa osakkeet 135 dollariin kappaleelta, mikä nostaa Elon Muskin raketti- ja satelliittiyhtiön pörssidebyytin poikkeukselliseen kokoluokkaan. Lähdetietojen mukaan yhtiö myi 555,6 miljoonaa osaketta ja keräsi osakemyynnillä noin 75 miljardia dollaria ennen suunniteltua Nasdaq-listautumista.

## Listautuminen tuo SpaceX:n Nasdaqiin

SpaceX:n on määrä aloittaa kaupankäynti Nasdaqissa tunnuksella SPCX. Hinnoittelu ilmoitettiin yhtiön verkkosivulla julkaistussa päivityksessä, ja osakkeiden markkinoinnin kerrottiin alkavan pörssissä perjantaina. Toisen lähdetiedon mukaan yhtiö julkaisi tiedon torstai-iltapäivänä.

Osakehinnan perusteella SpaceX:n arvostus olisi noin 1,77 biljoonaa dollaria. Se nostaisi yhtiön heti maailman arvokkaimpien yritysten joukkoon ja lähdetietojen mukaan seitsemänneksi suurimmaksi yhdysvaltalaiseksi yhtiöksi. Arvostuksen kerrotaan ylittävän muun muassa Metan sekä Muskin toisen tunnetun yhtiön Teslan markkina-arvon.

## Anti ylittää aiemmat ennätykset

Listautumisen mittakaava on poikkeuksellinen myös suhteessa aiempiin suuriin pörssidebyytteihin. SpaceX:n keräämäksi ilmoitettu 75 miljardia dollaria ylittäisi selvästi Saudi Aramcon vuoden 2019 listautumisannin. Paketissa olevissa lähteissä Aramcon annin kooksi mainitaan sekä 24,9 miljardia että 29,4 miljardia dollaria, joten vertailu osoittaa joka tapauksessa suuren eron.

SpaceX tunnetaan raketti- ja satelliittiliiketoiminnastaan, ja listautuminen avaa sijoittajille suoremman tavan osallistua yhtiön kehitykseen julkisilla markkinoilla. Hinnoittelu asettaa yhtiön yhdelle kaikkien aikojen suurimmista listautumisurista, kun osakemäärä, osakehinta ja arvioitu markkina-arvo lasketaan yhteen.

## Musk nousee huomion keskiöön

Kaupan koko lisää samalla huomiota Elon Muskin varallisuuteen. Yhden lähdetiedon mukaan näin korkea hinnoittelu voisi tehdä Muskista maailman ensimmäisen biljonäärin. Väite riippuu kuitenkin yhtiön arvostuksesta ja omistusosuuksista, joten se kuvaa ennen kaikkea listautumisen poikkeuksellista taloudellista mittakaavaa.

Yhtiön kerrotaan myyneen 555,6 miljoonaa osaketta ja keränneen noin 75 miljardia dollaria.
